gate_1_no_port_no_change.claim: an apparatus with no port, with ports={} and with an all-default CommandPort() builds the same program, its derived hash and canonical text the same (design section 9, control 1), on the coil-array sphere and on A0's apparatus

prediction.why: a port is staged only where a rung is not ideal; planted, a stage is built for the ideal port and adds a node and two edges, which the hash and the text both hold

gate_1_no_port_no_change.metric: caught/N of the planted arm, flagged/N of the clean arm

control.plant: every command port staged, an ideal one included
control.resolution: a node more in the graph: the hash and the text are exact

gate_1_no_port_no_change.if_wrong: a miss is an ideal port building a stage: the unused path is not free
gate_1_no_port_no_change.cannot_discriminate_if: the planted stage were built and its node left out of the derived graph; the canonical text lists every node

gate_2_a0_latency.claim: a command port of one base step's latency on A0's arm, which its controller writes inside the compiled step, changes the derived hash and moves the swim speed (design section 9, control 2)

prediction.why: with the latency dropped the port is ideal and builds no stage, so the two programs are one program and the swim speeds are bit for bit equal

control.plant: the port's latency left out of its plan
control.resolution: 64 units in the last place of the swim speed's scale, above which the clean arm's difference must lie

gate_2_a0_latency.if_wrong: a miss: one step of the arm's link does not reach the body in 40 steps, or the stage is built without delaying

gate_3_misplaced_stage.claim: a command stage the order puts after its receiver, inside the loop a controller closes through it, is refused by the lag accounting (lag.unplanned): the ported loop builds only with its stage between writer and receiver (design section 9, control 3)

prediction.why: the stage's edge into the coils then reads the previous step and carries a command, which no start-of-step read plans

control.plant: the coils' command stage moved after the coils in the order the loop is built in

gate_4_command_rungs.claim: the command stage delivers its rungs in the design's order (sample, delay, bound clipped or tripped, slew) against a NumPy oracle written from that order, within 64 units in the last place of the inputs' scale over 24 steps

prediction.why: a drawn square wave leaves the bound and comes back; where a draw holds a bound and a slew that bites, slewing first then bounding delivers another value at the step the wave returns, by up to the slew's step; an unlatched trip delivers the command again once it is back within its bounds, by the command's own size. Of 100 examples a run, about a third hold a clip and a slew and about a third a trip

control.plant: the bound and the slew swapped (slew_before_bound); the trip unlatched (trip_unlatched)
control.resolution: the difference a plant makes is at least a tenth of the bound wherever it acts, against a tolerance of about 1e-4 of the scale in float32

gate_4_command_rungs.if_wrong: a miss is a run whose 100 examples held no draw the plant changes: the strategy is too narrow
gate_4_command_rungs.cannot_discriminate_if: slew and delay are swapped: both are time-invariant from the rest, and commute; no plant is made of that swap

gate_5_measure_rungs.claim: the measure stage samples, delays and ages exactly as the design says: what it delivers at count n is the sample of count k floor((n - L) / k), the source's start before, and its age n less the count that sample was made at

prediction.why: the comparison is exact (array_equal); a clock one step short delivers another sample wherever the latency is not zero, about seven draws in eight; an age read as zero is wrong at every step

control.plant: the shared clock one step short of its latency (latency_short); the age counted from the delivery (stale_age)

gate_6_projection.claim: Camera.project is OpenCV's projectPoints with the camera's model: within 1e-3 px in float64 and 2e-2 px in float32 of the documented equations written in NumPy

prediction.why: dropping k1 of 0.05 to 0.2 moves a corner point by k1 r^3 fx, about 0.1 px or more at the field's corners; swapping focal lengths 5 % apart moves a point 40 px off-centre by 2 px; the inverse rotation sends most points elsewhere

control.plant: no distortion; the focal lengths swapped; the inverse rotation

gate_6_projection.cannot_discriminate_if: every drawn point lay at the principal point, where neither distortion nor focal length acts; the points are drawn over the whole detector

gate_7_ledger_look_through.claim: the energy ledger books a command a metered receiver pairs, delivered through a port's stage, under the command's writer (the drive), as without the port

prediction.why: without the look-through the torque is booked under the stage, which supplies nothing, and the line naming the drive's supply is absent

bits.cases: A0 (tests/script_a0.py) in float32 and float64, script A in float32 and float64, the tutorials A and A0 in float32, 100 steps each with every field's history, base release/v0.3.0 against this head in one job, one CPU, one BLAS and XLA thread (.github/probe/bit_compare.py); no port declared in any
bits.prediction: every array np.array_equal: no port, no node, no edge, so the compiled program is the base's

controls.moved: A0 with a one-step port on its arm on the head and none on the base: arrays differ (the comparison can fail)

costs.unused: the derived hash and the canonical text unchanged (gate 1): no node, no edge, no step cost, measured structurally
costs.used_prediction: a guess: A0 with a command port (one step of latency and a slew on the arm's six joints) and a measurement port (one step of latency on the body's pose, read by its controller) has two nodes more and adds a few hundred compiled operations to a step of several thousand, and its chunk takes under 5 % longer; the coil sphere with a command port (latency, bounds, slew on three currents) and a measurement port on its pose has two nodes more and its chunk, whose step is small, takes 10 % to 40 % longer
costs.measured_at: A0 at 40 steps a run and the coil sphere at 200, 20 steady runs a build and 3 builds a feature, off and on alternated in one job on one runner, with node_measure.py's trace counter; the operations counted in the optimised HLO of one compiled step (chunk_step), instructions outside fusions
